File `context.md`
**edulab** is a set of throwaway prototypes exploring how a user can *learn* from an agent that is doing their work for them, rather than passively watching it. See `notes/exploration.md` for the thinking and the prototype ladder, and `notes/studies.md` for the supporting literature.

Everything here is a demo, and the scaffolding constraints are deliberate. No database, no auth, no persistence, no configuration, no router. All state is client-side and in memory, discarded on refresh. The knowledge graph is likewise updated on every user interaction without asking: in any real version participation is elective and explicit (see the consent section of `notes/exploration.md`), and that is a stated constraint of the demo rather than an oversight. The backend holds no conversation state: it is a pipe from the websocket to the Anthropic SDK, and inference is streamed rather than awaited so the demo reads as a real agent session instead of a latency pause. The agentic loop is a heavily simplified take on `~/src/magenta.nvim` (anthropic only, api key only, no MCP); the web setup is lifted from `~/src/gatherus/`.

# Layout

- **`packages/iso/protocol.ts`** — the websocket message union (`ClientMessage`, `ServerFrame`). Imported by both sides.
- **`packages/backend/`** — Fastify server, entry `app.ts` (reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the root `.env`, listens on 3000). `socket.ts` registers `GET /api/socket` and is a **pipe**: it forwards the client's `MessageCreateParamsStreaming` to the SDK unexamined and streams `RawMessageStreamEvent`s back. It holds no conversation state.
- **`packages/frontend/`** — entry `main.ts`, which mounts `prototypes/chat.ts` into the page. There is one prototype and no router; later ideas land as new actions inside it rather than as separate pages. The sample picker lives in the header bar next to the layer navigation, and switching sample is a full page load.
  - `prototypes/chat.ts` — owns the thread tree, the state, and the single dispatch loop.
  - `conversation.ts` — the `MessageParam[]` plus the stream accumulator. Model, max tokens, and the system prompt are module constants here. The system prompt is deliberately **task mode**, not tutoring: learning mode is what we layer on top of the transcript it produces.
  - `view.ts` — the transcript and composer. `vamp.ts` is copied verbatim from gatherus.
- **`packages/e2e/`** — Playwright specs (`.spec.ts`, so vitest's `packages/**/*.test.ts` glob ignores them).
- **`docs/transcripts/`** — synced magenta thread archives, raw material for the prototypes. Refresh with `npm run sync:transcripts`.
- **`notes/exploration.md`** — the framing. What the learning problem actually is, why the obvious moves (student modeling, agent-as-tutor) are traps, and what we are deliberately not building. **Read this before proposing a direction or adding a prototype.** The numbered prototype sketches at the end are the roadmap.
- **`plans/`** — implementation plans, annotated with what actually happened as each stage landed.

# Commands

- `npm run dev` — vite on **5173** plus the backend on **3000**. Open http://localhost:5173. `/api/` (including the websocket) is proxied.
- `npm test` — vitest, node environment. The only unit tests are over the stream accumulator.
- `npm run test:e2e` — Playwright on its own ports (5174/3100). UI specs stub the socket with `page.routeWebSocket`, so they need no API key; `smoke.spec.ts` hits the real API and is skipped without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- `npm run sync:transcripts` — re-run `scripts/sync-transcripts.sh` to pull magenta thread archives whose `cwd` is this repo into `docs/transcripts/`. Incremental: existing threads are updated in place, so it is safe to re-run any time.
- `npm run typecheck` — `tsc --noEmit` across every package. Always run this rather than a bare `tsc`.
- `npm run lint` / `npm run lint:fix` — biome.

# Conventions

**Use the type system.** Disjoint unions over optional fields, exhaustive switches, branded ids. Prefer nominal/branded types over bare strings wherever a string is really an identifier — including map and record *keys* (`Record<ToolName, Tool>`, not `Record<string, Tool>`).

**Simplicity over abstraction.** This is prototype code with a short life. Write the concrete thing; do not build a provider abstraction or a plugin system for a second case that may never arrive. `@anthropic-ai/sdk` types are used directly rather than wrapped.

**Explicit over silent.** `RawMessageStreamEvent` is an open union we forward verbatim, so unhandled variants `console.warn` rather than throwing — but "we chose to ignore this" and "we have never heard of this" must be different branches (see `conversation.ts`).

**Single dispatch per prototype.** Each `prototypes/*.ts` owns one `dispatch` loop that calls `update` then `view.sync`. Views never hold their own dispatch. See the **[vamp skill](.magenta/skills/vamp/skill.md)** before writing any view code.

**Tests sit beside the module they assert** (`conversation.test.ts` next to `conversation.ts`), not beside the transport that reaches it. Views are verified in a real browser via Playwright, not jsdom.

**`~/src/magenta.nvim`** is a reference implementation for the agentic loop (`node/core/src/providers/`) if this outgrows itself. Do not copy from it wholesale.

</context_update>

## Answer: Full Methodology Narrative for WildChat Sample Selection

### Dataset Source
The 10 samples in `packages/frontend/samples/` were sourced from **allenai/WildChat-1M**, a publicly available HuggingFace dataset containing 1.7 million rows of user-LLM conversations collected from ChatBot Arena (where users interact with various LLMs). This dataset was chosen over alternatives (lmsys/lmsys-chat-1m was gated/private; AgentTrove considered as a larger 4× comparison baseline) as the primary candidate source for ecological validity.

### Data Fetching Method
- **Access method**: Anonymous fetch via HuggingFace's `datasets-server` `/filter` endpoint (no API token required; no full parquet download needed)
- **Filter criteria**: `turn >= 20 AND language = 'English'` applied to the `allenai/WildChat-1M` dataset
- **Initial pool size**: **1569 conversations** matching the turn and language filters
- **Fetching strategy**: Implemented `scripts/fetch-wildchat.mjs` (Node.js script using HF datasets-server filter API) which paginated through results in chunks of 100, with retry logic for index warming delays. Full fetch took considerable time due to HF index initialization overhead.
- **Data structure retained**: `{hash, model, turns, messages: [{role, content}]}` — stripped of moderation flags, IP headers, and other metadata

### Initial Sampling & Filtering Stages
1. **First-pass sampling**: Took random samples of ~50 conversations (multiple iterations with seeds 101, 19, 2024) to assess candidate quality and identify exclusion patterns
2. **Identified junk clusters** (to skip): ~20% of top-ranked results were "CONSTRAINTS: ~100k word limit for short term memory" system prompts (pasted Auto-GPT configs) and mega-genre-stack fanfic prompts — these were filtered out
3. **Crude quality observation**: Initial random samples had ~10% hit rate for "usable" transcripts; this informed the ranking strategy

### Selection Ranking & Filtering Criteria
The **critical ranking signal** was: **longest of the first 2 user messages** in each conversation
- Rationale: Observed that shallow/poor candidates opened with single-word utterances ("hi", single quiz items, or "rephrase the following") while substantive work tasks opened with dense, multi-line problem specifications
- Ranking method: Sorted pool by `max(len(user_msg) for user_msg in first_2_messages)` in descending order
- Result: Hit rate improved from ~10% to roughly **50%** once junk clusters were removed

### Final Selection of 10 Samples
From the ranked pool, the following 10 samples were hand-selected (skipping CFO personas and repetitive patterns):

1. **80e08978** — gpt-4-1106-preview, 21 turns, 42 msgs — Quantum Espresso BURAI relaxation on TiO₂ (materials science)
2. **5b878a60** — gpt-4-1106-preview, 26 turns — Solidity GuildToken audit (blockchain)
3. **37734816** — gpt-4-0125-preview, 25 turns — ColBERT Raptor RAG design (ML/NLP architecture)
4. **357dee9a** — gpt-4-1106-preview, 20 turns — StatsForcast with zero constraints (forecasting/time-series)
5. **aa0cb918** — gpt-4-1106-preview, 23 turns — StatsForcast Polars series lengths (forecasting, longitudinal pair with #4)
6. **44bbcae8** — Tile adhesive C1T formulation (materials/chemistry)
7. **72c7ec37** — Django event app URLs (web backend)
8. **74979366** — Floating dock pontoon buoyancy design (engineering)
9. **3890541b** — Aspen HYSYS chiller system modeling (chemical engineering, high engagement at turn 36 with user pushback: "but what if...")
10. **9833484b** — C heap file block storage implementation (systems programming)

### Selection Criteria Applied
- **Turn count**: 20+ turns minimum (agentic interactions require multi-turn dialogue)
- **Task domain diversity**: Deliberately included non-coding (chemistry, materials, engineering, forecasting) alongside coding domains to avoid prototype brittleness
- **User engagement markers**: Preferred conversations where:
  - User opens with substantive problem specification (not "hi" or generic quiz question)
  - User demonstrates domain confusion or learning (asking clarifying questions, pushing back on model, catching model errors)
  - Model and user iterate toward a solution (not just single-turn Q&A)
- **Artifact presence**: Prioritized conversations with tangible deliverables (code, formulations, calculations) over pure discussion
- **Model diversity**: Mix of gpt-4-1106-preview and gpt-4-0125-preview (no gpt-3.5, as they yielded lower-quality task clarity)

### Notable Rejections
- 20+ "CONSTRAINTS: ~100k word limit" system prompt injections (pasted jailbreak attempts)
- Mega-genre-stack fanfic/roleplay scenarios (fantasy worldbuilding, OmoDroid interactive fiction)
- Quiz item repetition transcripts (multiple-choice tests, essay grading rubrics)
- "Pretend to be a Linux terminal" and similar meta-prompts
- Single-domain repetition (skipped 2nd/3rd similar e-commerce product ranking transcripts)

### Licensing & PII Notes
- **WildChat licensing**: Publicly available under dataset terms (non-commercial research use implied by HuggingFace hosting)
- **PII handling**: Some conversations contain names, addresses, or email-like data (e.g., "Gou Lingqiao," resume snippets). These were **retained as-is** in samples (not anonymized in the prototype), with the understanding that this is demo-only, client-side, in-memory state discarded on page refresh
- **No real user consent**: Per the exploration.md framing, the prototype is deliberate scaffolding; in a real system, participation would be explicit and elective

### Outcome
**10 static fixture files** (21–76 KB JSON each, totaling ~1.3 MB) committed to `packages/frontend/samples/` and frozen for reproducibility across all prototype iterations (1–4), ensuring all UI comparisons operate on identical task content rather than regenerated samples.

content.text:
The sourcing was: **allenai/WildChat-1M** on HuggingFace (real users talking to GPT-4-class models through a free chat interface — note the subagent's claim that it's Chatbot Arena is wrong; WildChat came from HF Spaces chat demos).

Method, as recorded in thread `01a06fe2-9750-7150-8898-a2438b7ee2e2`:

- `scripts/fetch-wildchat.mjs` pulls via the anonymous `datasets-server/filter` endpoint with `turn >= 20 AND language = 'English'`, paginating 100 rows at a time. That yields a pool of **1569 conversations** out of 1.7M rows, keeping only `{hash, model, turns, messages}`.
- Random samples of ~50 had roughly a **10% hit rate**. Two junk clusters dominated: pasted Auto-GPT "CONSTRAINTS: ~100k word limit" system prompts, and mega-genre-stack fanfic/roleplay prompts.
- The ranking signal that fixed it: sort by the **length of the longest of the first two user messages**. Real work opens with a dense multi-line problem spec; junk opens with "hi" or "rephrase the following". With the junk clusters removed this took the hit rate to about **50%**.
- From the top of that ranking, 10 were hand-picked for domain spread — deliberately not all coding: Quantum Espresso relaxation, Aspen HYSYS chiller, tile adhesive formulation, floating dock buoyancy, Solidity audit, ColBERT/RAPTOR RAG design, two StatsForecast threads, Django URLs, C heap file storage. Preference for transcripts where the user pushes back or visibly gets confused, since that's where learning would happen.
- Frozen as static JSON in `packages/frontend/samples/` so every prototype iteration compares against identical task content.

Caveat before you write it up: PII was not scrubbed, and I'd verify the WildChat license terms (AI2 ImpACT / ODC-BY variants) yourself rather than taking the thread's word for it.
